hostedSupplyPath.inputType: V3SuppliedOwedFact[] -- hand-built per case by the harness
hostedSupplyPath.whyUnresolvedType: string (NOT nullable) -- §185 did not change this type
hostedSupplyPath.promptHeading: UNRESOLVED FACTS IDENTIFIED FOR YOUR REVIEW
hostedSupplyPath.note: the filter is NOT what keeps settled facts out of the hosted prompt; the harness simply never builds one, and the template could not express one if it did

fullLedgerCarriers.runOwedFactCoverageStage attachment: carries ledger.facts UNFILTERED, including settled facts -- but it attaches to a merged RESULT and is gated behind the literal false. It is not a provider input.
fullLedgerCarriers.OwedFactObservabilityRecord.initialOwedF: carries the full initial set, including settled facts. It is an append-only development RECORD, not a provider input.

conclusion: NO existing path carries a settled owed fact to a provider. The two full-ledger carriers are both outputs/records, never request inputs.

findings.question: does the standard projection carry a settled fact?
findings.observed: settled ledger projects 0 facts; unresolved ledger projects 1
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED: settled facts are filtered out entirely

findings.question: if a settled fact is supplied and the provider declares BOUND_BY_CLARIFICATION, what happens?
findings.verdict: the terminal-status guard is the thing that fires

findings.question: what does each declaration mode do to a SUPPLIED SETTLED fact?
findings.verdict: no exception is thrown and no status moves. The declaration is REFUSED WHOLE, which is a safety property rather than a crash -- but it also means a provider cannot say anything admissible about a settled fact through the existing protocol.

findings.question: does every supplied key carry a mandatory declaration obligation?
findings.observed: checkBindingAdmission raises OWED_FACT_NOT_DECLARED for any supplied key without a declaration (owed-fact-binding.ts:300-302), so supplying a settled fact COMPELS the provider to declare on it
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED by source; a settled fact cannot be supplied passively

findings.question: can a provider declaration reach SETTLED_BY_EVIDENCE?
findings.observed: applyAdmittedDeclarations mints only to COVERED under ADMITTED_BINDING (owed-fact-binding.ts:352-357). SETTLED_BY_EVIDENCE requires ADMISSIBLE_EVIDENCE, which no provider path mints.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED: provider settlement authority remains NEVER

findings.question: if a settled fact were passed to the prompt builder, what does the provider read?
findings.observed: "UNRESOLVED FACTS IDENTIFIED FOR YOUR REVIEW |     unresolved because: null"
findings.verdict: DECISIVE: the template hard-codes the heading "UNRESOLVED FACTS IDENTIFIED FOR YOUR REVIEW" and the line "unresolved because: <value>". A settled fact is represented AS UNRESOLVED, and its null renders as the literal "null". No existing text path can say "already settled".

findings.question: what distinguishes a settled from an unresolved member in the projected eight fields?
findings.observed: {"rows":["HR-04","HR-10"],"settlementDiffers":true,"projectedFieldsThatDiffer":["whyUnresolved","evidenceSpan"],"note":"only whyUnresolved and evidenceSpan differ; factKey, branches and decisionDivergence are identical"}
findings.verdict: whyUnresolved (null vs sentence) and evidenceSpan differ. Nothing else does, and neither field NAMES the settlement state -- a null is an absence, not an assertion.

findings.question: can the owed property be identified from the projected fields without factStatement?
findings.observed: branchA="established: the fixed guard over the head drum nip point is currently secured sufficiently for safe operation"
findings.verdict: YES for these fixtures, but only because branchA/branchB were DERIVED from the factStatement at §185 and therefore carry it verbatim. That is a property of the derivation, not of the schema: a fact whose branches were authored independently would not carry it.

findings.question: does direct terminal-status construction create an unauthorized RUNTIME path?
findings.verdict: A PRODUCTION ledger WILL admit a model-sourced fact constructed directly as SETTLED_BY_EVIDENCE, with zero transition records. No provider can do this -- provider output flows through applyAdmittedDeclarations, which mints COVERED only -- so it is a CONSTRUCTION-SIDE gap, not a provider authority gap. For §183 it is inert: fixtures are built by the harness, not the model.
